purpose: T0.2 experiment: LoadBalancing=4 (Hilbert) vs production LoadBalancing=1, after the 126-bit key rework and T1.13 partitioner fixes

config.parameter_delta: LoadBalancing 1 -> 4 in the shadow parameter file (LoadBalancingCycleSkip=2, MinLevel 0, MaxLevel 50 unchanged)

baseline: t15-coolgate-r1/bench_B (sha 4051c0b7, LoadBalancing=1; Hilbert code paths dead there, so the code delta is irrelevant to the comparison)

verdict.correctness: PASS at class C0 vs the 3-pair envelope floor - mass sums within 10x identical-code noise, mesh bit-identical at every dump, 1 particle level migration (gate 10). Changing the balancer perturbs the answer no more than parallel nondeterminism.
verdict.wall_clock: 2212.3 s vs 2231.3 s baseline (-0.9%, single sample, near the ~1.6% node scatter)
verdict.phase_analysis: RH_PERF: rebuild grew 179.1 -> 208.5 s (loadbal 13.2 -> 42.3 s: the Hilbert balancer + post-reassignment grid migration; find/share/copy also up), while everything OUTSIDE rebuild got ~48 s (~2%) faster - the locality gain is real but currently offset by balancer overhead. This 5-step window includes the one-time migration away from the restart's stored greedy layout, so steady-state overhead should be lower.

recommendation: Keep LoadBalancing=1 in production for now. Revisit after T2.1 (particle-aware work estimate) - the balancer weights are still cells-only, which is where FOGGIE's imbalance actually lives; and consider a longer bench to measure steady-state churn. The Hilbert path is now correct and usable at production scale (was: OOB reads, overflow-garbled partitions, degenerate keys above level ~11).
